content: Additional imaging studies are frequently conducted in patients with hypertension to assess for potential damage to target organs. An electrocardiogram (EKG/ECG) is performed to detect the presence of left ventricular hypertrophy or silent myocardial infarction. A chest X-ray is utilized to identify signs of cardiac enlargement or evidence of heart failure. Echocardiography, or cardiac ultrasound, is employed to diagnose left ventricular hypertrophy and evaluate diastolic dysfunction.
